source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Record each failed accessibility check according to specific standards.
3. Use a standardized checklist.
4. Include details about the failure, such as the specific regulation violated.
5. Detail observations objectively and factually.
6. Cite the relevant accessibility codes and provisions.
7. Photograph the area of failure, including specific details like measurements.
8. Note any temporary or mitigating measures in place.
9. Document any ongoing or planned remedies to rectify the issue.
10. Include notes on the impact of the failure on building users.
11. Provide recommendations for compliance improvements.
12. Date and sign the report, verifying the accuracy of the information documented.
13. Archive the completed report securely for future reference and in case of inspection or audit.
14. Share findings with necessary authorities, such as building management, local accessibility boards, or landlords.
15. Keep track of any correspondence related to the failed checks to maintain a complete record.
16. Update the report if
